The Czech Republic is one of Europe’s least religious countries, yet it remains safe, organized, and peaceful. Do you think a society needs religion to preserve morality—or are laws, education, and personal responsibility enough? 🇨🇿🍺
Share your honest opinion below, and please keep the discussion respectful!

comments.text: 🏰 I love how Czechia doesn't need to be flashy to stay unforgettable—its old streets, pubs, and peaceful pace of life are enough.

comments.author: @RealLifeFilesDoc
comments.text: Watching this on a Saturday night from Phu Tho, Vietnam! 🇻🇳 The editing choice in image_3bfc5b.jpg is brilliant—showing the wide, massive expanse of the Old Town Square right as the voiceover talks about the tiny 0.5-meter alley that "only takes a few seconds to cross" [13:06] creates such a stark, cinematic contrast of Prague's architecture. To answer the pinned comment: The fact that Czech society thrives on personal responsibility and mutual respect rather than fear of invisible punishment [08:17] is fascinating. It proves that decency can be woven directly into the cultural fabric, independent of religious rituals. Outstanding documentary! 🇨🇿🎥
